title: Flagship Airlines 3379
summary: On approach to Raleigh-Durham, the captain became distracted by a cockpit warning light and incorrectly assumed an engine had failed. He initiated a go-around but mishandled the procedure, allowing airspeed to decay until the aircraft entered a stall. Despite the first officer's attempts to push the nose down, there was insufficient altitude to recover before impact 4 miles southwest of the runway threshold.
probable_cause: Captain Hillis misidentified a warning light as an engine failure, called for an incorrect go-around, and failed to follow proper procedures for stall recovery. The captain's history of procedural non-compliance and Flagship Airlines management's failure to identify and remedy training deficiencies contributed to the accident.

events.text: Flight cleared to land to which crew acknowledged; this was the final transmission
Captain became distracted by warning light and assumed engine had failed; called for go-around with increase in engine power
Two simultaneous stall warnings sounded and airspeed continued to decrease despite power increase
First officer pushed nose down following captain's command but insufficient altitude remained to gain speed
Aircraft entered rapid descent up to 10,000 feet per minute and impacted ground 4 miles southwest of runway threshold, bursting into flames
